title: The corridor of three doors
goals: Reach the mark in the arch at the top.
starting_code:
door = wizard.find_nearest("door")
door.open()
wizard.move_up(4)
door = wizard.find_nearest("door")
door.open()
wizard.move_up(4)
door = wizard.find_nearest("door")
door.open()
wizard.move_up(4)
hints: We can make this much shorter with a loop! Look at the lines that repeat.
The three lines that repeat can be put inside a `for` loop with `range(3)`.
Remove all the extra lines and keep just one block of three lines under your `for` loop!
intro: Look at this straight corridor... there are three doors, exactly alike and the same distance apart! I wrote a program to open them, but it is nine lines long. I bet you can do it in fewer lines with a loop. The mark is in the arch at the top.
outro: Wow, only four lines! A loop is so much better.
learned: Now you know that a loop repeats its lines, so three doors take four lines, and that `door` is each time the next door.
